h1: Find a public ArtStation portfolio by username
intro: Search for a public ArtStation portfolio using an exact username, then review the candidate at its official source. This guide covers public profile lookup, verification steps and the limits of a matching handle.

sections.heading: What a public ArtStation portfolio can show
sections.body: Use the official page to confirm the account type, current handle, and information the owner chose to publish. The ArtStation portfolio is a distinct public page type; confirm that the resolved URL actually belongs to that page rather than a similarly named post, group, or search result. A username result is a starting point for a self-audit or authorized review, not a complete record of the person behind an account.

sections.heading: Coverage and limits for ArtStation
sections.body: The checked-in MyRecon standard catalogue lists ArtStation. This is a username-level check, not a guarantee that every request will resolve: service changes, rate limits, privacy controls, or temporary blocks can leave a result unknown. A missing or blocked result cannot establish that no account exists. Do not work around login walls, access controls, rate limits, or service restrictions to force a response.

sections.heading: Verify a candidate before you rely on it
sections.body: Open the canonical ArtStation page, note the URL and observation date, and compare one or more independent details that are voluntarily public. A reused or renamed handle, a similarly named portfolio, a redirect, or a stale search snippet can create a false lead on ArtStation. Open the official destination and compare independent public context before attributing it to anyone. Keep uncertain and unavailable outcomes marked as unknown.

faq.question: Can a ArtStation username match prove who owns it?
faq.answer: No. Handles can be shared, changed, or reassigned. Open the public portfolio and look for independent, voluntarily published context before making an attribution; if evidence is inconclusive, leave the match unresolved.

faq.question: Does this find private ArtStation profiles?
faq.answer: No. This workflow is limited to supported checks and information available on public pages. Private accounts, login-only material, blocked requests, and hidden membership data are not exposed by a username lookup.

faq.question: What should I do if a ArtStation result is unavailable?
faq.answer: Record the check as unavailable or unknown, then use ArtStation's official search directly if appropriate. A timeout, redirect, or access block is not proof that the profile is absent.

platform.privacy_overview: A public ArtStation portfolio can show only the fields its owner and the service make visible, such as a chosen name, image, biography, posts, or outbound links. Private areas and access-controlled content are outside a public lookup.
platform.false_positive_note: A reused or renamed handle, a similarly named portfolio, a redirect, or a stale search snippet can create a false lead on ArtStation. Open the official destination and compare independent public context before attributing it to anyone.

manual_steps: Open https://www.artstation.com/ and use its own public profile search or the exact handle URL when the service documents one. Search only a username you own or are authorized to review; this guide does not cover private-account discovery.

Open the candidate portfolio page and confirm the destination is a current ArtStation account, not a generic error, unrelated result, or search-engine snippet. Save the canonical URL and the date if you need a reproducible self-audit.

Compare a separate, voluntarily public clue such as a self-linked site or matching biography before drawing a conclusion. A handle alone can be shared or reassigned, and blocked checks should stay unknown rather than being recorded as a negative.
